title: East African Campaign of World War I
note: Four-year guerrilla campaign across German East Africa, Mozambique, and Northern Rhodesia between German askari forces under Paul von Lettow-Vorbeck and Allied Empire forces; resulted in the mobilization of over a million African carriers and an estimated 100,000 carrier deaths from disease and exhaustion.

title: International Congress of Women at The Hague
note: Over 1,100 women from warring and neutral nations gathered in The Hague in April 1915, presided over by Jane Addams, to protest the carnage of World War I, propose diplomatic mediation, and establish the Women's International League for Peace and Freedom (WILPF).

title: Deployment of the Indian Army on the Western Front
note: The rapid mobilization and deployment of Indian Expeditionary Force A into the Ypres and Neuve Chapelle sectors in late 1914, providing one-third of British infantry strength on the Western Front during the critical initial stabilization of the trench lines.

title: Chinese Labour Corps in World War I
note: Approximately 140,000 Chinese workers recruited by the British and French governments to provide logistical, trench-repair, and munitions support behind the Western Front under harsh contract conditions, suffering thousands of fatalities from shellfire and the 1918 flu.

title: March First Movement in Korea
note: Mass nonviolent Korean civil demonstration against Japanese colonial rule ignited by Woodrow Wilson's Fourteen Points declaration on national self-determination following the end of World War I; met with severe military suppression by Japanese authorities.
